current_example.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since $E_1A=U,$ we can invert $E_1$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$
